path.data-text: Quill is a small rich-text word processor for the PCs of 1992 to 2000: fonts, lists,
tab stops, headers and footers, pictures, a spelling checker and a real help file,
in a program that fits on a floppy and runs in 4 MB.
It comes as separate programs for separate machines. QUILLDOS.EXE runs on
DOS, QUILL.EXE on Windows 3.1 and 3.11, and QUILL32.EXE on Windows 95, 98
and Me. One Rust core drives all three, so a letter typed in blue-screen DOS
opens with its fonts on Windows 3.1, and in LibreOffice today.
Quill is the companion to Cross-compiling to the past, a blog series on Liminal
HQ about the toolchains it is built with.
Every build has run in emulators, virtual machines and Wine only, never on real
hardware. Windows 98 has not been tried, and anything may change from one
